headline: Sequence models link viral sequence features to host origin and immune escape
label: Viral Genomic Sequence Modeling
summary: Predictive sequence-level models now pair evolutionary inference with explicit host, protein, and vaccine-effectiveness readouts across viral taxa.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational inference from viral sequence to phenotype, evaluated against host, immune, or epidemiological readouts. Influenza dominates the preprints: ESM-2 protein embeddings predict host tropism across nine animal families, and WaveSeekerNet predicts host source across all eight segments (macro F1 0.9728) while linking G/C versus A/T codon usage to host origin. Other work prioritizes k-mers for strain discrimination, models epistatic drivers of HLA-dependent CD8+ T cell escape, and examines Japanese encephalitis virus envelope mutations. The published study links spike amino acid distance to time-varying SARS-CoV-2 vaccine effectiveness via a Bayesian model. What is new is the shift toward predictive, sequence-level models coupling evolutionary inference to explicit protein- or host-level outputs across viral taxa.
